proposal.title: Zimkalquel: a verifiable key directory
proposal.summary: Zimkalquel builds a verifiable key directory for users of encrypted messaging.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Users are not able to see whether a server swapped key of a contact. Users of encrypted messaging are depending from key transparency every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We are going to build a verifiable key directory called Zimkalquel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Key transparency belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We are maintaining http://forge.test/zimkalquel/zimkalquel, which 128 public projects depend on. Our team is working on key transparency for 8 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under MIT licence in http://forge.test/zimkalquel/zimkalquel. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 10.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 65850.00 EUR for 105 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 700.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Users are not able to see whether a server swapped key of a contact. Users of encrypted messaging are depending from key transparency every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We are going to build a verifiable key directory called Zimkalquel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Key transparency belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We are maintaining http://forge.test/zimkalquel/zimkalquel, which 128 public projects depend on. Our team is working on key transparency for 8 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under MIT licence in http://forge.test/zimkalquel/zimkalquel. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 10.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 65850.00 EUR for 105 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 700.00 EUR.
